answer: Registration binds each identity to a unique hardware credential plus a 500-unit bond escrowed in a shared registry, so every agent maps to one credential and one escrow record. Forging one identity locks that 500-unit bond for 20 epochs, and proven duplication slashes 100 percent of the stake. Splitting or copying identities costs a fresh bond per copy plus the shared penalty, and independent jurors auditing the registry flag duplicates on the fable, knoll, and horizon records alike.
